facts.text: Oxford was founded in 1761 when Samuel Benton built a plantation home named Oxford, and the legislature made it the county seat of Granville County.
The town was officially incorporated in 1816 after the Assembly authorized buying land around the courthouse in 1811 and selling lots in 1812.
Oxford hosts the first Masonic orphanage in the U.S., opened in 1851 as the Oxford Orphans Asylum, now the Masonic Home for Children.
In 2018 Oxford earned accreditation from the National Main Street Program, a recognition by the National Trust for Historic Preservation.
OxForward, a 501(c)(3) organization, leads downtown revitalization while preserving historic character, guiding new upper‑story development in historic buildings.
The town’s historic downtown features a diverse mix of shops, restaurants, housing, entertainment venues, and even a brewery, reflecting its vibrant community.
